utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. May I ask Madam Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is case number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMIJIAN
utterances.text: Nicholas Karper and -- Nicholas Koumjian and Ruth Karper for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I just wanted to congratulate.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. John Ostojic on behalf of Dr. Milomir Stakic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So I don't have the chance to congratulate Mr. Lukic, having been elected as a secretary of the Defence Union, but good to know that we have also a secretary in our room from now on. And first of all, I am more than happy to know that, as you all can see, once again we are sitting together in the composition of three Judges, but I think it's necessary to start in an acceptable way for all of us, and let us first clarify how to proceed today. It will not be possible for Judge Fassi Fihri to attend the afternoon meeting, and there are two possibilities: Either the parties accept, that, only for this afternoon, we proceed under 15 bis, or we would proceed in the framework of a Status Conference, as we did earlier, and then try to have an overview on this overwhelming material we have received until Friday, late in the evening, and then to introduce this in a kind of package solution into the case, as we did it earlier. I think the most facilitating way would indeed be to proceed with some matters under Rule 15 bis, and then we would have to decide what to do. May I hear the observations by the parties, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would hope that we could finish Ms. Tabeau this morning. I hope that's not too optimistic. But if that's the case, than I think it might be better for Mr. Sebire, who is a very short witness - and actually, his preference is to further prepare - that we could call him on Thursday and that we -- but if we have to proceed this afternoon with Ms. Tabeau, I don't know if it's possible to break it up into a trial and 15 bis procedure or just finish her tomorrow. But I know Mr. Ostojic indicated -- I'm having trouble with names today -- indicated that he would like to talk to Dr. Stakic sometime.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. We'll proceed in the manner best for the Court and the honourable Judge Fassi Fihri. We did receive today a copy of Madam Tabeau's report in B/C/S. I've tendered it to Dr. Stakic. We are prepared to proceed and question her. I don't believe that the questioning will take more than an hour and a half to two, but again it all depends on the rapport that we can develop with her during the question and answer session. I'd like to have a staff conference. There are a number of issues that I'd like to discuss with the Court and I think it's necessary both for purposes of scheduling as well as projecting the next several witnesses and how we hope to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So I think it's a clear message that we proceed with the hearing only this morning and then with the witnesses to come tomorrow and the other days, and leave this afternoon for all these procedural issues and try to start introducing and attaching exhibit numbers to the new incoming documents. And if it's convenient, then present it as a kind of package solution, once again, into the hearing tomorrow. Can we --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I just wanted to inform Your Honours of one other matter, is that tomorrow there is a representative of the government in question regarding the next witness planning to fly here and be present, so if we don't finish for some reason the witness, we would ask to proceed out of order with Mr. Brown so that to accommodate that special representative.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We're prepared, so we have no objection to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we have to be flexible in the next five days and we proceed in the spirit shown until now, I have no doubts that we will succeed. So therefore, for the registry, we proceed with our hearing only until 1.00 this morning, and start at 2.30 a Status Conference. And then the parties may know that also tomorrow we sit in Trial Chamber -- in courtroom 1. On Wednesday, we'll sit also the entire day in courtroom 2, from 9.30 until 4.00. Yes, about 4.00. But the entire day courtroom 2. This intimate atmosphere will facilitate the hearing maybe. Then it's mandatory under Rule 70(E) to provide a report, and this report will be filed, but for the reasons given earlier, I want to read out slowly this report now in my capacity as Presiding Officer on the last deposition taken. It reads: "Report on deposition evidence under Rule 71(E) of Rules on Procedure and Evidence to Trial Chamber II. Composed of Judge Wolfgang Schomburg, presiding, Judge Mohamed Fassi Fihri, Judge Volodymyr Vassylenko. "On 11 September 2002, Trial Chamber II, acting under Rule 15 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, in the absence of Judge Fassi Fihri and with the consent of the parties and the accused, ordered that deposition evidence pursuant to Rule 71(A) of the Rules be taken in respect of certain witnesses. I was appointed Presiding Officer for that purpose, and Judge Vassylenko was permitted to be present in the courtroom. The procedure was to cease upon the return of Judge Fassi Fihri to active duty. "In accordance with the order for deposition evidence to be taken pursuant to Rule 71 of 11 September 2002, the following depositions were taken: Edward Vulliamy, from 16 to 18 September 2002; Dusan Baltic, 18 to 19 September 2002. "A record was made of the depositions in the form of full transcripts which have been transmitted to Trial Chamber and are to be incorporated into the trial record. There were no objections raised during the depositions by other party for decision by the Trial Chamber. Documents tendered during the depositions were assigned provisional reference numbers, and it is proposed that these be admitted with exhibit numbers as follows: Edward Vulliamy, DP2, S 328, three pages of notes; DP3, S329, video V000-0664; DP3-1, S329-1, transcript of video; DP4, S330, video V000-0401; DP5-1 to DP5-8, S331-2 to S331-8, these are notes regarding Mr. Kovacevic. DP6-1 to DP6-7, S332-1 to S332-7, these are notes regarding Dr. Stakic. DP7, S333, video V000-0662. DP8, S334, chapter 5 of "Seasons in Hell." DPD1, D25 "Shame of Omarska." DPD2, D26, pages 8 and 9 and 100 to 101 of the book "Seasons in Hell." DPD3, D27, the article "Face to face with victims of his horror." DPD4, D28 aide memoire, February 1996 meeting. Dusan Baltic: DPJ1 --" maybe here there's a mistake. J 3. Shouldn't it read something else? Document with 65 ter number 271, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It was labelled DPJ1 initially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. And then the next available J number would be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Not 1, but 13. "DP9, S2-1, a map. DP10, S335, letter to Simo Drljaca, signed by Mr. Baltic; DP11, S336, minutes from Crisis Staff, 13 to 14 May 1992." May I ask the parties: Are there general observations on this document? And especially because now under the Rules it's the time for the question whether or not documents be admitted into evidence. Are there any objections to the suggested proceedings? OTP, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Generally we do not have an objection. I do have a comment, if I may, Your Honour, or an observation. One of the exhibits, at least from what I was able to follow, on the DPD list seems not to be included in that, from memory, is the February 2002 article that was written by Mr. Vulliamy in the Bosnian institute journal. I believe that we asked some questions about that and that it was actually tendered, so I'm just not sure in following the Court respectfully whether that's included. I note that the Court did include the 1992 and 1996 articles but we had, I believe at that time, moved for that article as well for admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Correct. May I ask Madam Registrar: Maybe there was an omission at that point in time, because we discussed it whether or not it was an article from the Bosnian institute or, better, a reprint from article having appeared earlier. Was it in the Bosnian journal? I don't know. But no doubt it was. Could the parties agree that -- in order that we don't have to repeat this entire report, you tender this document now and the OTP agrees that this document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We have no objection. I think it was a reprint from a Guardian article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. From Guardian, yes, right. Yes. We all know what we are discussing, and I can see Madam Registrar has a report already available. Could we please hear what would be the number of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D29, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: D29. And please both parties, don't hesitate, if you identify that something is not included, let me immediately know and then we proceed on this basis. But this is not -- forms not part of this report. It's now admitted today into evidence, and it will be distributed. Judge Fassi Fihri in part is already and will be later on totally informed when he's had the time to read all the documents and summaries and transcripts on what was going on, both under Rule 71 and under Rule 15 bis, that as soon as possible he also will be aware of we discussed during the last three weeks and what was the outcome. Are there any further objections or observations to this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we can proceed this way: This report will be filed and, as mentioned, if you take it or regard it as necessary, please tell me when it's on the admission of additional evidence. We'll do it this way. If one of the parties does regard it as necessary to comment on the one or other evidence taken in the absence of Judge Fassi Fihri, it's the time today or tomorrow to address this issue or give comments on this evidence in order to have also available for Judge Fassi Fihri not only the assessment of the colleagues and the legal officers but also your observations and your assessments of the evidence taken in the absence of Judge Fassi Fihri.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. There is a confusion. The article from the Bosnian institute was already marked, D27. So for the record, D29 is not attributed to this article.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The article, "Face to face with the victims of his horror." This would be in fact this Bosnian institute article. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I would agree. I have no reason to doubt Madam Registrar. We'll go over it, if we may, because there were actually four particular items, so if I would just have that as an option during the break and then we'll clarify. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have an entire week on these issues. Anything else to be changed what we know already? No? I can see no -- so then may I ask the usher to escort today's witness into the courtroom. Can we agree that this is regarding Ms. Tabeau from now on as a new witness. This is not a continuation of the former statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Correct

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Tabeau. Can you hear me. 23

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As this is not a continuation of your former testimony in this case, may I ask first of all that we please hear your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. Mr. Koumjian

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Tabeau. You've previously testified and have told the Court what your qualifications and training and experience is; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you in your work for the Office of the Prosecutor prepare a report entitled "Basic demographic characteristics and socio-economic status of missing and killed persons from Prijedor"?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: 30 April through 30 September 1992?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And is that report dated the 9th of September of 2002?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And I believe the registry has a copy of that. May that be given an exhibit number. We will tender that report.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is exhibit S 337.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Doctor, just to remind you, because of the translation, and particularly since we're talking about some technical matters, if you would pause after I've finished a question before you begin your answer, so that the interpreters can catch up. Dr. Tabeau in going over your report that has been submitted, is it correct that you have identified certain areas that you wish to have corrected in the report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Starting at page 3 in the section entitled "2.1, Absolute Numbers"?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is the section.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And specifically, the second paragraph lists certain figures for the ICRC for what's listed as KNP, or the Prijedor Book of Missing Persons and for the Exhumations and Proof of Death database; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. These numbers should be corrected [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Please, again pause a few seconds before you begin your answer. The ICRC numbers are correct; is that true?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. These numbers are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: For the Book of Missing Persons, the KNP, can you read the correct figures?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The first figure should be 1.088 instead of 1.092, and the second figure should be 1.953 instead of 1.122.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you give the correct figures now for the Exumations and Proof of Death database, the EXH figures?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The first figure should be 638 instead of 960, and the second figure should be 1.122 instead of 1.953.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So in fact, of the total linked records, you simply had -- you had misplaced -- you had put the exhumation records for the Book of Missing Persons and vice versa, and those need to be reversed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. This is one correction. But also the numbers, total numbers reported for KNP and for exhumations are slightly different, the new numbers, the other totals were totals for the whole 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, in this paragraph it lists these totals, but further on in your report you use figures to make your calculations. Is it correct that the figures you used to make your calculations are the correct figures, the numbers you just gave, and that they simply were listed incorrectly in this second paragraph under 2.1?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. The analysis is based on correct numbers and only in the discussion in the text some mistakes were made.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: On page 7 of your report there appear two figures, figures 2 and 3, and they indicate that these are rates per 100.000 population in ARK. Do these figures relate to the Autonomous Region of Krajina or to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Both figures are made for Prijedor. The reference population is the one of Prijedor and not the one of the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So to correct that, would it be correct on the headings for figures 2 and figures 3 to replace the word "ARK" with "Prijedor"?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Going now to page 11 of your report, in the paragraph -- I believe it's the third paragraph, towards the bottom, you list categories of occupations, and the sentence reads: "It allowed us to classify the population among the following five categories," and then you listed four categories. Was one category missing from that list?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. One category is missing from this list. This is the category of employees that should be mentioned as the second category after inactive population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And going to the second-to-last line on page 11, you indicate that in Prijedor there were a total of 665 [sic] men and 65 women who went missing or were killed during the indictment period. Does the figure for men need to be corrected?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The figure for men should be 1.666 instead of 1.665. Just a difference of one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Again, is it correct that you used the correct figures, in other words, the 1.666 in your calculations and that the error is simply in the text on page 11, as far as the number being wrong?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It is again the same situation. Error in the text and correct figures in the analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I want to go over the sources that you used to make this report. Is it correct that you utilised three different databases?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. I used three sources. One first source was the list of missing persons completed by International Committee of the Red Cross, ICRC list of missing persons. Second one, is the Prijedor Knjiga Nestalih the Book of Missing from Prijedor. And the third source, is the Exhumations and Proof of Death database. Sometimes I call this database exhumations database --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, we have a problem with the transcript. If we could pause for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Will there be an additional or substitution of this report, including the new numbers for the purpose of the registry?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, that can be done, Your Honour, easily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We would appreciate that at least in that what we have under S337 reads correctly. Unfortunately, we have to wait until the transcript works again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Keep going and it will be fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify, then, we don't have to go back to the point where it froze and go over those questions again? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I believe, if my memory is correct, that we were just talking about the sources. You mentioned two, but the first one was a list of missing persons by the ICRC. Can you tell us the date of the version of that list that you have?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The version we used for this report is the fourth version of the ICRC list. It was published in June 1998, and for the whole Bosnia and Herzegovina, the list included approximately 19.000 names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And you were just telling us about the third list, the Exumations and Proof of Death that you indicated you sometimes referred to in your report as the exhumation database. Would it be correct --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. This is the third list that we used for this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Would be it correct that this is a database that you utilised that was put together --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: To be fair to all participants, I just learned that the transcript will stay frozen until five minutes. No doubt then we have -- we will keep up with everything what is reported until now. But we haven't available immediately the text. May we nevertheless proceed? I can see no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The Exhumations and Proof of Death database, is it correct that this was a database compiled by Nicolas Sebire of the Office of the Prosecutor from court rulings on proofs of deaths, declarations of death in Bosnia, and lists of persons exhumed and identified in exhumations conducted in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. This is the database established under the supervision, say, of Nicolas Sebire OTP investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify, in your report, when you list individuals exhumed, is it correct that because your report, it's necessary to identify those individuals, you are only referring to individuals exhumed and identified or those who have had declarations of death? In other words, you are not utilizing bodies exhumed, but not identified; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. The report is very specific regarding the death, date of death, and name of the person who went missing or was killed. We needed both items: Date of death and the name. All persons whose name was unknown or date of death was unknown or incomplete were excluded from our study. The numbers are quite considerable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In this project for this report, did you again utilise the technique of linking the individuals identified to the 1991 census in the same or similar manner to which you did to prepare your earlier report regarding the changes in the population demographics of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We used the same technique, matching, individual matching, with the census, all sources, the three sources I mentioned were linked with that census. Moreover, the sources were compared with each other in order to exclude duplicate records, and we also compared our lists of missing persons and killed persons with the voters register, and in this way we could exclude records inconsistent, those reported missing or dead but still included in the lists of voters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So would it be correct, then, that among the individuals excluded from your analysis would be individuals that you could not for some reason link to the 1991 census, perhaps because the date of birth was not available or other information sufficient to positively identify the person?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. Certain number of records from the lists of missing or dead were not linked with the census. Approximately, say, 20 per cent, for different reasons, one of them being the reasons you mentioned, another one of just spelling mistakes in the names that make it very difficult to link different lists with each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You indicated that you used only those individuals who it could be determined had died between the 30th of April and the 30th of September, 1992. Is that correct, that you excluded all others who you had a different date of death for, a date of death outside of that period?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. The date had to be within the mentioned interval in order to include a record, given record in the analysis. Unfortunately, there were dates of death that were incomplete, so all deaths, for instance, from 1992 where the month of death was missing, to be excluded as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So when you received an incomplete date of death or no date of death, did you -- that person was then excluded from your database; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. Such persons were excluded from the databases used in this study.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Then you indicated that you did a second exercise to remove duplicates from among the three databases; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. We merged the lists with each other and looked -- compared the records on these merged lists, and once we saw that one record was repeated more than one time, so all the duplicated records were excluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Excluding all those for whom you could not identify and link to the 1991 census, those persons whose dates of death could not be determined or it could not be determined that they fell within the indictment period and removing all duplicates, is it correct that you ended up with a total of 1.731 individuals from Prijedor who were killed or went missing during the indictment period?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. This is the total we ended with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Looking at page 6 of your report, of that total of all ethnicities, looking at table 2 of page 6, of the 1.731 individuals, is it correct that 1.651, or 95.4 per cent, were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And again I believe you testified concerning the ethnicity categorisation in your first testimony, is all of the ethnicities listed based upon a person's self-reporting in the 1991 census?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. Ethnicities -- an item taken from the 1991 population census.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And to remind us, is it correct that the category "others" that you have listed includes anyone who identified themselves as being a Yugoslav, for example, or of other ethnicities in Prijedor, such as Ukranian or Roma, they would all be listed under the "others" category or "check"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Of the 1.731 who died during the indictment period, how many were of Serbian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: There were only four persons of Serbian ethnicity that we found in this list of 1.731.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'd like to now turn to page 10 of your report. Is it correct that you did a similar analysis for other municipalities including the Autonomous Region of Krajina and that the results of these municipalities - I believe there are - I believe 19 for the Autonomous Region of Krajina listed here, these are presented in table 4 on page 10 of your report.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. We see, in table 4, 19 municipalities from the ARK Autonomous Region of Krajina, Prijedor being one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: This table indicates that 3.010 individuals appear in your database. Is it correct, first of all - I should caution - is it correct that this database is slightly different in that it covered the period 30th of April through 31st of December 1992?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I think that the period is just the year 1992. This is the whole 1992. And the sources are slightly different. Knjiga Nestalih, for instance, is not used here for Prijedor. Only the ICRC list of missing persons and Exumations and Proof of Death database are used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that of those in this database who were identified as having died in 1992, 58 per cent were from the municipality of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And now I want to discuss other exercises, analyses that you did. Did you then take the list of those persons - there's 1.731 individuals that you identified as having died in 1991 - excuse me, during the indictment period 30th of April through 31 December 1992, and attempt to do some analysis of --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Excuse me. I don't have anything on my screen. Perhaps someone can help me. Oh, I see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you look at those individuals and, using data from the 1991 census, analyse the educational level, the level of education of those individuals, and also the occupational group in which those 1.731 individuals belonged?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. We analysed the -- those missing and killed by educational level and also occupational status.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you describe how you did that? Can you just briefly explain it? First for education.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We analysed the census item educational attainment by restructuring slightly the categories reported by the respondents. We analysed variables that had the following categories as responses. First category, no education at all; second, incomplete elementary school; third, elementary school; fourth, middle school, which is secondary school; fifth, higher or university education; and two categories in school, meaning continuing education and missing values were excluded from the analysis. It is also important to note that we only looked at a subgroup of the population, at the group of those at age 18 or more years, in order to minimise the bias related to the fact that age, as such, can imply that a person is in education still. We wanted to use the same 8 classification in both analysis for education and also occupational status. Persons at age 18 or more can become occupationally active, so this was a sort of compromise that allowed us to present, to complete a comparable analysis for the same population group. With occupational status, we analysed two census items. The first one was occupational activity. The item called ZAN. This is a variable name reported in our data files. The variable occupational activity allowed us to distinguish between those occupationally active and those inactive. And the second item we included in our analysis was occupational position. This variable called PZAN in the data file allowed us to distinguish between employees, owners, self-employed, and those who helped the self-employed, the household members who worked with them. We constructed a new variable. This new variable included all occupationally inactive as one population group, and then it included employees, owners self-employed, and their help, as the following categories. We called this new variable "occupational status." So starting from those inactive and ending with variable ended with the two upper status category, categories, first one being owners, second one self-employed, with their help. For these two variables we analysed risks of going missing or being killed. The results of this analysis are presented in section 3 of my report, first on page 12 and 13 we see the results of the analysis by education, and on page 14 to 16 we see the results by occupational status.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Would it be correct that in your analysis you did not find a link overall for non-Serbs for the correlation between educational levels and the risk of going missing or being killed in 1992?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Generally we didn't see a systematic pattern of increasing risks of going missing or being killed associated with the increase in educational categories. The educational categories like secondary school, those who completed secondary school or post-secondary education, didn't have unquestionably the highest risks of being killed or going missing. So this is the answer to your question: We could not see an obvious pattern of targeting related to the educational attainment of the Prijedor population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Would it be correct that that pattern, however, does emerge if you took Croats alone as a single group?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. The simplest way to get an impression of how such a pattern should look like and how it looks like for Croats is the figure 4A and 4B on page 12. The blue line, I hope that you can see colours. Not -- the line which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think we all have coloured copies.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: You do. Okay. So the blue line is the one for Croats, and then you can see how this line increases with the increase in educational categories. So those with no education at all or incomplete elementary education have the lowest, very small risks of going missing, being killed, and those with post-secondary, who completed post-secondary education, have unquestionably highest risks. The line for Muslims, the green line, the uppermost line, is different. It is clear that those with post-secondary education do not have the highest risks of going missing, being killed. There is still certain increase in the risks with the increase in education and education level observed for Muslims as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And just to remind us: Again, these are the risks of the overall population as it existed in 1991. So, for example, if people with post-secondary education were perhaps smart enough to leave Prijedor prior to being detained, they would show up on your report simply as someone who was -- they would lower the risk of death of that group; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. This would certainly lower the risk in this group.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You were not able to, for example, look at the solely the persons detained in camps to see the link between education or occupation and the risk of being killed; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, we did not this type of statistical information at our disposal, and the purpose of this report was to analyse missing and killed population from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I now want to turn to the statistics that you mentioned regarding occupational status. Is it correct, if we look on page 15, at table 6A, And at page 16 at table 6B, the difference between these is that table 6A includes men and women and table 6B is only men; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Looking at the figures under the last portions of each table, deaths per 100.000 population, would it be correct to interpret these figures as -- if you divide the figure by 1.000, this is the percentage of these persons who were identified in the 1991 census who were also identified as having been killed in Prijedor within the indictment period? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So, for example, if we take the figures for Muslims on table 6A, deaths per 100.000, would it be correct, then, that among the inactive occupational group, 2.934 per cent were killed or went missing in the indictment period?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Among employees, 5.359 per cent were killed or went missing in the indictment period?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: For owners, approximately 6.7 per cent; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: For self-employed, approximately 6.64 per cent?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And for those with self-employed with help -- and by that - correct me if I'm wrong - "self-employed with help" means that person has employees that they pay or has employees that assist them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Not exactly. The "help" are other household members working together with the self-employed person and not necessarily being paid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Among this group, 9.56 per cent were killed or went missing in the indictment period, if we look at men and women as a group in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. But we generally analysed these two last categories - "self-employed" and "help to self-employed" - together as one category, because these two groups belong together. This is just self-employed and their families who helped them in their work, so they worked just together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If we now turn to the next table, 6B, on page 16, which again is limited to men only, only to males. And if we again look at the Muslim population, would it be correct that - I'll go through them from "inactive" up to "help to self-employed" - the figures increased, the percentage, the risk -- the percentage of those from the 1991 census identified who were also identified as having been killed in the indictment period went from inactive 6.8 per cent, employees 10 per cent, owners 11.6 per cent, self-employed 11.3 per cent, and help with self-employed 26 per cent. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. Only the first figure should be 6.9 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: 6.9. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Please remember to pause. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I now just want to briefly touch upon your regression analysis. In the regression analysis, you looked at these factors of occupation. Let's look at table 7 on page 17. You did a logistical regression in order to determine the effect statistically of being a member of an ethnicity and a particular occupational group upon the risk of being killed or going missing during the indictment period; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And is it also correct that you used as a baseline the group of inactive others?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. This is the reference category used to compare all other categories to show how many times the risks observed for other categories are higher or lower in relation to the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And just to again remind us: The "others" category would include not only other ethnicities, such as Albanian, Ukranian, Czech, but it would also include persons who declared themselves as Yugoslavs, perhaps a Muslim married to a Serb; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. "Others" contains first of all Yugoslavs. This is the major component of this ethnic group. And the other categories are as you mentioned

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So if we look at the regression analysis -- let's take it for men and women. If we look at Muslims -- by the way, the significance level, the lower it is, the more significant the result. In other words, the harder it is, the more unlikely that this would have been obtained by chance; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: As far as the exponent on the regression analysis, would it be correct that this would indicate that, for example, Muslims self-employed with help, your analysis showed that these persons were approximately six times more likely to be killed or go missing during the indictment period than the baseline group, the others inactive; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. This is how these figures should be interpreted exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You did not compare Muslims in this analysis to Serbs directly; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: However, you did compare Serbs to the baseline group; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And your figures for Serbs indicate that they were much, much less likely to go missing or be killed in the indictment period than those in the others inactive category?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, because the estimated parameter is lower than 1. So this simply means a risk that is lower than the risk observed for the reference category.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So if in fact you had used, for example, Serbs, employees, as the baseline, the exponent for Muslims would have been much higher than it is when you used the others category; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is the implication.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, did you also attempt to make some estimate from your data of the total number of persons who went missing or were killed in Prijedor in 1992 using a statistical tool known as the capture-recapture method?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, we did. In this way, we wanted to address the issue of the character of our total of 1.731 missing and killed persons. This is an at least number. This is a minimum number, and we must be very clear about that. We -- by estimating the capture-recapture unknown total number wanted to stress that the actual number is much higher than what we were able to produce on the basis of the three sources used in this study. And the estimated total is higher than 1.731. The total estimated is 2.190, and we believe it is still an underestimation of the true total, that we are unable to present in terms of lists of persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll ask, Mr. President, for your guidance. Would it be possible for me to have an easel, which is just outside the courtroom, be brought in so I could put in some figures and some demonstrations in front of the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please do so. May I use the time, because we have to make a decision today on the addendum I don't want to mention, the one of a sentence. The addendum to Prosecution's false motion for specific protective measures. Can the OTP agree that when it reads that persons be present in court during the testimony, it reads: "In their capacity as amici curiae."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. I think though, Your Honour, to be accurate, the person will be representing the interests of his own government as amici curiae.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. And finally, that because it's not mentioned in the conclusion in B5, also there it goes without saying, as it was said before, the Trial Chamber will then rule on the submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Observations by the Defence? Is it correct for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, we don't consider that individual as an amicus curiae. We consider him in a totally different light. So we do not object to that categorization at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Indeed we would appreciate and then on this basis it's -- it is agreed as requested. Thank you that we could use the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: May I proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Ms. Tabeau, I just would like try to explain this capture-recapture method using some very simple figures so we can get an intuitive sense of what that is. Let's say we were trying to measure a small town which has an unknown population. We don't know it, but the real population is 1.000 persons. And we had two samples. Someone had counted everyone wearing blue and they found that 400 individuals were wearing blue. Someone had also counted the number of persons with college degrees and found 100 persons had college degrees. But we don't know when we start just from these two samples is that about 40 per cent of people in this town wear blue and about 10 per cent from college degrees; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is what we know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We would expect the overlap, in other words, the two samples, to include each other, that a person has both a college degree and blue, to be 40 persons; correct? So in other words, about 40 per cent of the college people are wearing blue and about 10 per cent of the people with blue have a college education, so the overlap is 40. Again, we don't know those percentages now. All we know is we have these two samples. If we were using only these two samples, in order to estimate the total population of the town, what would the formula be?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: For the capture-recapture method?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So the total would be the size of the first sample, which is 40.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Sorry. 400. The other one is -- the other sample is 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And would you multiply those together?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. You would multiply the two and divide it by the overlap, by the size of the overlap, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If you did that, you would come out with 1.000 as the population --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: -- of the town?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, the capture-recapture method does have a premise that the samples are independent of each other, as you state in your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Because if they are dependent, then if one is dependent on the other, then it could result in an underestimate of the total population; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. So the estimate obtained under the independent assumption uses the formula as the one you mentioned. While it is not necessarily the case when the samples are dependent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I want to explain, give an example, of how an underestimation could occur. If we had first that same sample of 400 with blue and we had a second sample of the number of persons wearing denim in the town, we had 100 persons wearing denim, in fact we know the two are not really independent, because most people -- most denim is blue, maybe 80 per cent; is that correct? Let's assume it's 80 per cent. So if 80 per cent were of denim was blue, then we would expect the overlap to be 80; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And if we used your same technique, the capture-recapture method, then the formula would be 400 times 100 over 80, or only 500?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You would underestimate by one half; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. I'm done with the easel.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The conclusion is that statistically speaking if samples are dependent than the estimate produced under the independent assumption does indeed underestimate the total number, and this can be shown statistically in a sort of proof as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The three databases that you used were the ICRC list, the Prijedor Book of Missing, and the Exumations and Proof of Death database, that is, persons exhumed and identified and those for whom a family member had gone to court and obtained a declaration of death; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that all three of these would systematically exclude situations where, for example, all members of the family had been killed or where the only surviving members of the family were perhaps out of Bosnia and not able to report their family members missing, did not come to make an identification at an exhumation or go to court to get a declaration of death?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, of course these situations are excluded, these reports are excluded from the lists used in this report. But not only these reports are excluded. I said in the beginning of this testimony that there were many reports in the lists we used that had to be excluded because of date of death or missing was incomplete or missing altogether, or the name of person was not given. We couldn't use these records in linking these records were very, very frequent. For instance, in Knjiga Nestalih, for Prijedor, in total this list included 3.146 records, of which 1.350 did not included the year even of death. So we -- the year was completely unknown, which is a huge portion of the list that could not be analysed in our study. With exhumations, the year was unknown for 652 records in the whole database. Out of a total of about 3.000 records in the database, which is again a considerable portion of information that was not used in our study. So this is another reason -- the excluded records is another reason that the figures used for the capture-recapture method are very low, and of course the result is likely also not as it should be if the figures would be more complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I believe you indicated it should be seen as a minimum, very conservative estimate; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I suggested, and I agree, fully agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'd like to turn just to page 4 of your report, figure 1, for a moment. We've talked about the effect of there being a positive correlation among the databases in getting an estimate that is possibly too low. If we look at the overlap on the databases, is it correct that every person who is exhumed and identified, or that individual was declared dead because family members went to court, appeared either in the Book of Missing or in the ICRC list, or both? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And wouldn't that indicate that the process of a family member coming to make an identification or going to court to get a declaration of death, that that family member is also likely to report the person missing in one or both of these sources? Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is what we see here in this data, in many, many instances, and this is the logical, I think, behaviour of those who lost their loved ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, if we chose -- I understand the data normally gets better the more sources you use; correct? You normally want to have as many different databases as possible, but it's also necessary for the accuracy of the formula for them to be independent; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, we -- first of all, we have to use the best possible information that is available, but also we have to remember that for this method sources should be independent, and the probability of being reported in every one of the sources for every individual is the same. So these are the two assumptions of the method. In this case, we intuitively know that the sources were not independent but likely dependent, but it is only intuition. At this stage, when the lists are completed we cannot say anything about how these samples were drawn, and we cannot measure the dependency of the samples. This is what I can answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If we took the capture-recapture method and excluded the exhumation and court declaration database, we would then use the same formula we did for the people wearing blue in the small town. We would multiply the total samples of the Book of Missing Persons times the ICRC list and divide by the overlap; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. This would be the formula, as the one you used already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. So that would be the KNP sample times the ICRC sample, divided by overlap. And the overlap, looking at the figure 1, would be 157 plus 263, or 400. Is that correct? 420. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: 157 plus 263, 420. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. This is 263. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So the total would be -- the formula would be 1.092 times 1.063 divided by 420. And I believe that comes out to 2.763. Would that be the formula that you would use if you excluded the exhumation and court declaration database?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It is -- I didn't make the calculation, but it seems that you did it correctly, and if the result is correct, this is what we would obtain, a much higher number than what we were able to produce.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further -- excuse me. When you testified last time, His Honour Mr. President asked if you were preparing a report on all of Bosnia, and is it correct you did prepare and submit a report for the Krajisnik/Plavsic case dated the 20th of July?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. I completed the report and submitted it, I believe also to the registrar of this case, and I hope Your Honours received copies of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Would Your Honour like me to mark that report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's now tendered as S338.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Are there any objections against the admission into evidence of S337 and S338.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No to the former, yes to the latter. Namely, we do object to Exhibit S338, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I hear the reasons?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's a report that deals with items that are outside the parameters of the fourth amended indictment against the accused Dr. Milomir Stakic. It's a report that I think is prepared - with all due respect to Dr. Tabeau who is sitting here - which is skewed, that we are not, and only having received the report today, although there is some disagreement as to when it was tendered to cross-examine around this report. The indictment clearly against Dr. Stakic involves Prijedor. We have a report on that. We have questioned her once and we will hopefully do so again this morning. We don't believe that it's relevant to the indictment. There's been no explanation as to why this report should not have been included with her prior report, and how it now has any bearing or relevance to Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. No doubt -- yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Ms. Karper informs me that our records show the Defence got this report on the 2nd of August. It was written -- it's dated the 28th of July and our records show it was delivered to the Defence. I know Mr. Ostojic wasn't here the 2nd of August, but on the 2nd of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But the reasons given as maybe obstacles to the admission into evidence, the Trial Chamber will decide on S338 only later. As regards S337, it's admitted into evidence in the form we have it now updated, including the corrections to be found in today's transcript, and once again, I kindly ask the witness to give at least one original with these corrections to the registry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial stays adjourned until 11.40.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, just the last time Ms. Tabeau testified, Dr. Tabeau testified, there was one document, S227, which was partially illegible, listing the census breakdown by municipality. We found a much better copy of that, and it's not the same page, but the same census results, and we have that to distribute or to substitute for S227. Dr. Tabeau actually provided it to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think for the purposes of clarification, we should have this as an addendum to S227 and be marked as 227-1. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence S227-1. May I ask the Defence to start with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Tabeau. Again, my name is John Ostojic, on behalf of Dr. Stakic. I read your report, and thank you for providing it. I think I understand it. I'm a little frustrated by a couple of items, both in your report and during your testimony on direct examination involving the socio-economic status of individuals in the Prijedor area within the time period of April 30th through September 30th of 1992. Mr. Koumjian from the OTP, specifically on page 14, line 20, seemed to indicate, and I think your testimony was that there was a 20 per cent range that you would attribute to persons who were excluded from the numbers in your calculations. Correct? Meaning, in essence, that the number is understated; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Meaning that the list used for the capture-recapture method and other analyses are incomplete, lower than the total number of records reported by approximately 20 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's where the frustrating part comes in. If you look at the capture-recapture method that you utilise in your annex, in fact the numbers statistically as you've computed them indicate that there's an excess of a 25 per cent overstatement of those numbers using the capture-recapture method specifically, if you look at the real raw data, as I call it, of 1.700 approximate individuals and if you calculate that or compare it to the capture-recapture method, you get approximately 2.100 of such individuals; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. This is the new total, approximately, 2.100 and something.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So in fact by utilizing that method or, as you call it, a tool, in your methodology, the capture-recapture method there's actually an overstatement of the exact number based upon your very own calculations, correct, of more than 25 per cent?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I am a little bit confused. So you are saying that this number, the 2.100, or 2.190, is an overestimation you are saying, because of the unlinked record not included in the calculation? This is correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In part, yes. But what I'm saying is that it's been well established that utilizing the tool such as the capture-recapture method will provide a statistician or a scientist or a demographer such as yourself an overstatement of the true picture in which you're trying to analyse.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This method is used to estimate the unreported events, and this is why we applied this method. The lists that we had at our disposal were incomplete, all of them. We knew that. And they were incomplete because of the 20 per cent you mentioned, the unlinked records, and also because of excluded records, the records with incomplete or missing date of death or unknown names. Generally, the lists were incomplete because certain records were not reported at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So based upon a reasonable degree of scientific, statistical, and demographic certainty, can you tell me which number would be considered, scientifically speaking, more accurate for purposes of determining the qualitative criteria necessary in this case, the 1731, the 2.789, or the 2.130 that comes out of the capture-recapture method analysis that you provide in your annex?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I believe that the number 2.789 is a number that includes duplicates, and we should not look at this number at all, because this is our least made of three sources by combining the sources, and nothing more than that. The number 1.739 is a list that doesn't include any duplicates, and this is a list that we can produce by showing names and other details, date of death, many other details about the victims, and this is an absolute minimum we should think of in this case. And the 2.000 estimate capture-recapture estimate, the 2.190 is that what we at least should expect as to the total number of victims, missing persons, killed persons, from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And if I may, the difference between 1731 and this 2190, do you make any assumptions as to the ethnicity of those missing people?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would you logically then take the percentages that you have prepared on table 4 -- strike that. Table 2 on page 6 of your report in order to make that determination?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: You could do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: When you do, as Mr. Koumjian did on this easel here, he actually showed you the basic, precise way of doing it on the first page. The second page he made an assumption which indicated that there was an underestimation of the total population 500. What would be the formula, if you will, to show that it was an overestimation of the total amount of victims, if we can call them that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, there are certainly many formulas that could be used for the dependent samples. The formulas would be specified on the basis of the type of dependency between the samples. And as I said, at this stage, when the lists are available, as they are, I am unable to say anything about the dependency of the samples. So we believe that by using the formula for independent samples, we are not fully correct, but still we cannot say anything more about a better estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But is it true, Doctor, that in making your report and in reaching some of your conclusions, in the socio-economic status of the two categories that you were asked to review, namely, educational attainment and occupation, that you used as a dependent source once again the 1991 census? Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We used 1991 census as the source for this part of the report, together with the three lists of missing and killed persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, we discussed at another portion of your testimony in connection with the separate aspect of your report the utter unreliability and untrustworthiness of reliance upon censuses by virtue of the fact that they have control mechanisms that were not utilised, among other things, the flaws, if you will, in a census. Did you, Dr. Tabeau, take into account any of those flaws in creating a margin of error upon relying on the census to reach those two conclusions with respect to educational attainment and occupation?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, after the discussion about the reliability of the census, I actually made quite some efforts to learn more about how the census was conducted and whether the way of conducting the census was as they should be. And I must say, after having requested two reports from people who were involved in the census, I believe that the census was conducted very much properly as they should be conducted in every country, and I can present to this Chamber reports of these local authorities, of those who were responsible and who were involved in the census in Bosnia and Herzegovina, from which it is clear that criteria of reliability were satisfied in the census as well. Well, you asked about -- the second part of your question, about margin of error with respect to educational attainment and occupation. I believe do you mean confidential intervals for the rates of risks presented or things like that? What are you -- do you think about with this -- in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I had a lot of thoughts on it. We can discuss it either way. In your last testimony, for purposes of our discussions, basically, and with all due respect, agreed that the confidence levels and the margin of errors -- margin of error can be used interchangeably. So for our purposes, if you can share with me what the confidence levels were, what the margin of error for utilising a census as a dependent source in making your determination that there was no targeting based upon the educational attainment category, then that there was supposedly targeting based upon the occupational socio-economic status report that you did.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We did not include any confidence intervals for the risks of missing or being killed, for any of these two items, not for educational attainment, not for the second variable, occupational status. But by estimating the regression models, we actually proved that the parameters for Muslims were all significant and the pattern of increasing risks with the increase associated with the increase in the categories of the occupational status is also seen there. So this is some way of speaking about reliability of these estimates.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll get back to the logistic regression model that you used, because I do have actually a couple of questions in connection with that. Respectfully, I dispute the way in which you in essence linked the two categories, but we'll get to that in due time. Is it correct that in your report you state that for purposes of occupational status, that each and every person who filled out the census specifically, and all of them, filled out the category as to what their occupation is?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Not all of them. There were two items in that census related to occupation, and this is explained on page 11. The first item called "Occupational Activity" was addressed to all participants of that census. Every respondent had to answer this question. And occupational activity, the ZAN variable, only served to distinguish between those active and inactive. And for those inactive, there were several possibilities Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 8426 to 8434. included as responses to this question. It was only a matter of choosing one by a given respondent. And the other variable, occupational position, PZAN variable was only addressed to those occupationally active to a subgroup of the respondents included in that census.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But my question is: For the ZAN category, the occupational activity, it's your position that the census information in your possession reflects that each and every household had completed the census, answered that category; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, this is what I know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, did you do any independent review of the actual census, since you have that data, to determine what percentage of a whole was this category completely filled out or not filled out? Because I find it personally incredible that in a census and that doesn't matter, it may very well have been completed by all, but in your experience have you ever found that the census form on a specific category other than name and address was completed totally by each and every participant in the census?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, it is usually the case that everybody respondent has to respond to all questions included in the questionnaire, and this is the responsibility of the interviewer to take care of this. And going back to the question about the categories reported in that census for this particular variable, for ZAN variable, we made some frequency tables, checking the responses, and as far as I remember, I cannot show you right now this frequency distribution, there was nothing striking in the distribution. There were categories, for instance, for children, that they were children in school, and therefore inactive, or there was a group of household keepers that were reported as inactive, and the reason was they were keeping household, you know. And this type of answers. There were some special groups, like imprisoned population, who was occupationally inactive because imprisoned. There were handicapped persons in institutions, inactive because handicapped. There were people retired, inactive because retired, et cetera. So this was not only distinction between active and inactive in general sense that this question was an opportunity to be specific about what type of inactivity was linked with a given person.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And those tables would be readily available if the Court would permit us to have a copy of that, to show the frequency of all the line items that may have been filled out within the 1991 census form that you provided us last time?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: If requested by the Chamber, we would make, of course, such tabulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention to page 6, table 2, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony, based upon this table and the information that you reviewed, that in fact only 4 ethnic Serbs were killed during the period April 30th, 1992 through September 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is this number for Serbs killed or missing were found in the three lists used for this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But did the OTP at any time share with you some reports that they have in their possession that we'll see from other witnesses, possibly even tomorrow, that in fact that number is far greater than the number 4? Did they share that with you?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No, not that I'm aware of at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And in fact, if you look at your statistical calculations in presenting the percentages specifically relating to the Muslims, where you have 95.4 per cent of the total, that number is, in my opinion - and you correct me if I'm wrong - skewed because if the ethnic Serbs that were killed within that period is greater, what would happen to the percentage as a whole of the Muslims in that category? The percentage would go down; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: All percentages would change slightly, depending on the number of Serbs, new Serbs, records, included in the database. It would be lower, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And why do you say "slightly"? Do you have an opinion as to --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how many Serbs would be included, additionally, into the database, but -- well, this is my first reaction. So I haven't found many Serbs, so I will be very surprised if rapidly I would be presented with a list where hundreds or thousands of Serbs would be included.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may ask you this: Within your report, do you include any ethnic Muslims who may have died outside the territory of Prijedor but who were citizens of the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. There were a few such persons. It is related to the fact that actually for this type of analysis, two different perspectives can be taken. One is the perspective the municipality of origin, or region of origin, or region meaning the 1991 census. Or the other perspective is the municipality of arrival, so receiving municipalities. We made this report using the perspective of municipality of origin because we wanted to present relative measures of risk, and in this case we should think of relating the number of victims to the 1991 census population. And alternatively, we could think of all victims who went missing or died in Prijedor without taking into account the municipality, their municipality of origin in 1991. And these two numbers are slightly different, of course, because these are two different perspectives.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that if you take your number of 1.731, and that if indeed it includes ethnic Muslims who may have died outside the territory of the Prijedor municipality, although within that time frame, that statistically speaking, your estimate of 1731 would be an overstatement of the number of victims missing or dead? Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It would be, but I want to stress that for deaths, we used the Exhumations and Proof of Death databases. Those were all based on information collected for a particular reason, Autonomous Region of Krajina, Prijedor being one of the most important municipalities in this region. And in Prijedor, the highest number of mass graves were found, and the bodies were exhumed from these mass graves. So there is no -- very little doubt about the place of death from this database. Regarding the list of missing persons, we have only little information about place of death, because the item reported in these databases, the location item, is the place where the person was last seen. But again, it was for the vast majority of cases that it was -- they were seen in Prijedor, in Prijedor, and in at most the surrounding municipalities of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking for the far majority of it, but I think if you take a calculation such as you did in utilizing a number of 1.731, and that if indeed you're trying to give us an objective analysis to tell us that of these people that are certain computations, methodology that we would use to determine that there was targeting it would be an honest assessment on your part to state, whether in a footnote or directly in the text of the report, to tell us that in fact this report does include a certain number of individuals whose origin are from Prijedor but who died outside of the municipality of Prijedor. Wouldn't you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I believe I made such a note in the report. If you allow me to find it. I am very consistent through the whole report by saying that we analysed those from Prijedor municipality, those victims from Prijedor municipality. As far as I remember, I made such a note, where I explicitly explained this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to direct my attention to it?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. This is on page 5, in section 2.2, second paragraph in this section, where we read: "In this section, we take the perspective of the 1991 place of residence of the victims and analyse all those victims who in 1991 lived in the municipality in Prijedor -- of Prijedor by relating the number of victims originating from Prijedor to the 1991 population of Prijedor, we can produce measures of the risk of being killed or going missing for the 1991 Prijedor population." And the footnote 6 explains: "Note that the place of death is available in our sources as the place where victims were last seen as place of disappearance, or as location of mass graves, or place of death or disappearance, indicated to court by the relatives of victims. A vast majority of places were consistently reported to be in Prijedor or surroundings of Prijedor."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's precisely my point. What is the vast majority? You're giving us a number of 1.731 as a concrete number.
