In your report, knowing just by virtue of these last several questions that there are instances where the number would necessarily be decreased if it's established, either by way of the exhumation report that Mr. Sebire put together by the OTP or any of the other sources that you utilised that in fact people whose origin in 1991 was in the Prijedor municipality may have died or did in fact die outside of the Prijedor municipality, what is the percentage? I understand that it's the vast majority, but as a statistician, by providing me with a margin of error on this particular number, 1.731, perhaps we can gain an appreciation for the relevance in a qualitative term in your analysis.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. I believe I made certain calculations to assess this percentage. It was an important question, while making this report. And I believe it was a percentage which was far higher than 90 per cent, far higher than that. And I want to stress that it is extremely difficult to be very specific in making these type of calculations, as I present in this report, because of the problems of the data deficiencies. If a person is found in a mass grave in the municipality neighbouring to Prijedor, does it mean that the person died in Prijedor or in this municipality? So it is a very, very difficult to be a hundred per cent specific about the place of death. But it is likely -- what we know for sure, it is that this person used to live in Prijedor and died. So the risks we calculated are for the Prijedor -- 1991 Prijedor population, and from this point of view, these are very correct measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So the confidence interval, if you will, is somewhere in the 90 percentile range, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It is -- confidence interval is a statistical term, if you would ask me to present a confidence interval, I would have to calculate it and then I would tell you it is a 90 per cent confidence interval, 95 per cent confidence interval. 90 per cent I mentioned is a measure, a fraction of those whose place of death or disappearance or location of mass grave was within Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When you say "problems with the sources," as you just did in your testimony, you're really referencing flaws and inaccuracies upon relying upon sources such as the 1991 census, the ICRC report, Knjiga Nestalih, as well as the exhumation database; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I don't like that you put census together with the sources which include information about missing persons and death persons. Census is a different thing, and it is a very reliable, complete source of information. With the sources like exhumations, we have this difficulty that it is -- the place of death is reported just as the location of the mass grave, still located, most of them, within Prijedor municipality. And there are deficiencies in the sense that many items are incomplete or missing in this list of missing persons or dead persons, but the difficulty I am speaking about right now is that it is not a matter of how the figures or the items were reported. It is sometimes hardly possible to report the place of death as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In addition to the situation that I mention of, namely, that individuals whose origin may have been in the Prijedor municipality and they may have died in a municipality outside of Prijedor, you mention two in your report on page 8 as the morbidity control mechanism as well as the - as you coin it - the accidental hump mechanism; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. May I say something about accidental hump, observed in each pattern of mortality for populations living under peace, normal times, not in conflict situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The accidental hump actually means, as a layperson such as myself, that there's a certain category within the population that sustains a death as an end result by virtue of an accident; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Accidental hump means that this is an increase in mortality rate that is caused by certain factors related to external causes of death.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Not natural?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Speaking medically. Not natural causes of death, if we can make this distinction, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The other section of the control mechanism that you use is the mortality table, because every population certainly has that, given any period of time examining any population, there will be some deaths from, as we've just described, natural causes; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. Natural causes are causes of death related to the ageing process of individuals, and these natural causes of death can be seen in increasing death rates, increasing with age, because of age-related diseases, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But looking at those two additional factors, what would your confidence level be of this section that you've identified as 1.731 people missing or dead in Prijedor within that time period?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I can not answer this question because it is impossible to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Why? Because these are two completely different things, confidence interval for the total number of 1.731, and the age pattern of mortality observed for populations living under peace.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So let me just understand it with respect to those three control mechanisms, as I call them, to determine the accuracy and the reliability of the data or the figure of 1.731 that you used. If a group of Muslims, ethnic Muslims, respectfully, were to have gone to a different municipality, let's say even to a different republic or country, Croatia, to fight, their origin is in Prijedor, they died during battle in Croatia. Your report, in essence, the 1.731, includes those individuals that may have perished outside the Prijedor municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I think you -- your suggestion is very extreme. I couldn't have information about those who died in Croatia or other countries because the sources I use for this report are related to the population who went missing or died, was killed, in the area, Prijedor area and ARK area. So these sources, especially Exhumations and Proof of Death databases, were established to estimate the scale of killing process in this particular area. Missing persons, on the other hand, Knjiga Nestalih, was completed in Prijedor, was initiated in Prijedor and coordinated from Prijedor, so it was basically established for the Prijedor population. ICRC list of missing persons has the most -- the broadest coverage of the three sources. It is the part of the list we used for this report. It's just records for Prijedor. So people who reported last seen in Prijedor and close surroundings of Prijedor were just taken. Only those who lived in Prijedor in 1991. So it is not as you are saying, that any death or missing person is included in our sources. The selection of sources is the basis for producing a dishonourable figure. This is how we should see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have two questions in connection with your last answer, but before I get to that, my question is: So your analysis and your figures are as reliable and accurate as the sources upon which you relied on; right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, in terms of coverage and the time period, geographical coverage and time, calendar time coverage. These are very much relevant sources from the point of view of this indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, you mention, and I know -- I didn't take it that personally, but you mentioned that my analysis or my suggestion was extreme by virtue of the fact that if individuals who were from the origin of Prijedor go to battle and fight in Croatia and die, how could it be possible that they would be included within any of the data sources upon which you relied. Dr. Tabeau, it would be possible because, in my opinion, if you look at the exhumation data or proof of death, the people who would be reporting, these individuals who had become deceased, are people from what origin? From the origin we said went to Croatia or Prijedor; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The origin was, of course, Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So it's not extreme to suggest that if a family of, let's say, 20 sent their young men to battle in Croatia and they all perished, the family members wouldn't go for Croatia to report the death, would they? They would report it in the municipality of Prijedor, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: They would report in the municipality of Prijedor, indeed, especially if the report would be made to the organs like vital statistics administration in this particular municipality that we are speaking about court declarations and exhumations. I cannot imagine that a person who died in a battle in Croatia would be found in mass graves in Prijedor or reported by a family to court, in Sanski Most or Kljuc. I cannot fully agree with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you don't have to, and I'm not going to suggest to you. Mr. Sebire's report clearly indicates that of the exhumations the 261 conducted of both the mass and individual graves, that in fact there were 600 or so that were individually identified, which is approximately 1.100 less than the data that you've provided. So in essence, we don't know the answer to that question, and I don't think anyone can get the answer to that question. But I'm suggesting to you is that the assumption that you're making relying upon that data, it's incorrect and because it's unreliable and inaccurate, that there should be a margin of error within your report to suggest that this number of 1.731 is indeed skewed by the percentage of your confidence interval. That's all I'm suggesting.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Right. By presenting the capture-recapture estimate, we first of all say that there are -- there were unreported deaths and missing persons that should be included in a report like this one. And secondly, we also estimated confidence intervals. So the confidence intervals are included in this report for this estimated total. And then you can see that we have two numbers, 2.115 to 2.265. This is the confidence interval for the total 2.190.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And again, I'm suggesting to you that utilizing tools such as the capture-recapture method is inaccurate because it gives an overestimation of the numbers, and in fact if you even compare the methodology used by the capture-recapture method, you yourself will find that your number of 1.731 would be a closer number to the true figures than by utilizing this tool known as capture-recapture by 25 per cent, if not greater.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I cannot agree with you that the capture-recapture estimate is an overestimation. I don't think it is an overestimation. It is an underestimation of the unknown true total. We don't know the true total. I don't know, and no one knows. I believe that the input used for the capture and recapture is very close to the number that we should think of -- a minimum number for Prijedor that we should think of, a minimum number of victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You're familiar, then, in fact, the capture-recapture method is considered outdated since its initial theoretical coming out, if you will, in the statistical area, coming out in 1940, and you'll also agree with me, will you not, that that method, capture-recapture, was utilised only for purposes of counting and calculating what the wildlife animals would be in certain areas? True or false?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I disagree that it is outdated. I think that we can find hundreds of variants of this method, including -- in our models, very modern technique that did not exist by 1940. So we could have used a more complex approach which would be certainly less clear to you here in this courtroom, perhaps also to us less clear. At least now by presenting a simple method, we all understand a little bit what are we talking about. And as I said, the intention is to speak about through numbers that are different from minimum numbers that we can show black on white, you know, like the number 1.731.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I'm trying to understand it. Let me direct your attention to table 6A if I may on page 15. Although our pages are not numbered. Page 15, I think, table 6A.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Under this occupational status category that you have, namely, the two that I'm going to focus on for our purposes here, the self-employed and the help to self-employed, from what I understand from reading your report if I may, self-employed would actually be, for example, in a household, the father of the household, the husband of the household; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It depends on what the person would be doing. It is mainly, I believe, farmers who are included as self-employed. And the aid, the help to self-employed, would be the families of the farmers.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So just if you could follow with this table for me, under self-employed, you have that there were 110 Muslims. Just under that category, out of 1.657; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Where this total comes from?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The next category in your table, 1991 population.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Then under the category "Muslims." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, I see that there were 110 Muslims, self-employed Muslims, who died or went missing, out of the total of 1.609 of all Muslims who died or were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So this is how it should be read.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sorry. And the next category, you have 13 Muslims with help to self --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Self-employed, and out of those, you also include 136. So out of those 136 that in the 1991 census identified themselves as help with self-employed, you've calculated that 13 of them have died; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if you compare that -- and this table is for both men and women; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And are we making an assumption here, since we separated the two categories, that the 13 individuals under the category of help to self-employed were women or men?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is both men and women, the certain individuals,

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if you look on your next table, the 13 individuals --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. It is only men.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: By comparing the next table on table 6B, the same 13 number under the category of help to self-employed appears; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So in fact we can conclude by looking at those two reports that it is only men; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So when I asked you whether this category of help to self-employed included men or women, you said both, but that only of those that identified themselves as men have actually perished. Would that be a fair read on it?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: It is also about the population as risk. So if you compare the 1991 population in these two tables, then you see that for Muslims in the first table, the total is 136, and in the other table it is 50. So the population at risk is used to calculate the rate, and this is why the rates are different. But in fact, it is men, the rate for men, which should be considered. But I think that it is good to realise that we did not analyse the help to self-employed as a separate category. This is a category that was analysed together with self-employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I realise that, and we'll get to that in a second when we do the logistical regression model that you use in your annex. Just so I could have clarification for my purposes. When you -- in each of your tables or in most of them, you have a category that says death per 100.000; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Like you do on table 6A. When you have that, although I think it's fundamental, I apologise for asking you that, in essence it's giving us a percentage per 100,000; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No. It is a number per 100.000. If you divide these numbers in the table, the rates, deaths, per 1.000, by 1.000, then you end with percentages.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me understand it, then. Rook on table 6A under "owners." Let's take a different category. You have under those individuals of ethnic background being Muslim who died under the category of owners, 32 died out of 479; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And if you continue to read your table on the next section, deaths per 100.000 population, you have 6681; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In fact, by utilising the term 100,000, all you have to do is move the decimal point three intervals to your left and you get the exact percentage. So if I were to ask you what is the percentage under the category of owners that died vis-a-vis the population in 1981 all you would have to do is to look on this section and say 6.6; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, it's that exactly, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, my problem with understanding --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the parties first to slow down and not to overlap. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In examining your logistic regression model and reaching the conclusion that there seems to be a targeting of occupational status in the Prijedor municipality within the time frame, am I correct in understanding that what you did was use as comparing the two the inactive status of one group and that of two other groups correct, namely, the group of self-employed and help to self-employed? Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, partly correct, partly incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Tell me the part that I was correct on first.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Correct is that two other groups, ethnic groups, were compared with inactive others, but we analysed the data by two variables at the same time, by ethnicity and occupational status. So the comparison we made is comparing ethnic groups, like Muslims and Serbs, by occupational position with professionally inactive others. So it is -- each ethnic group is analysed at the same time by occupational status.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but when you gave the testimony, I think during your direct examination and your report, that there was a four times more likelihood that someone who has an occupational status such as self-employed or employed with help and those with an inactive status, really what you're saying is that you did not include in that variable the other two categories that you identified in your report of occupational status; correct.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: In the regression model, the rates or risks of, say, Muslims and Serbs in certain occupational status, categories, are compared with the risk for inactive others, inactive others, inactive others. So this is the reference. So for Muslims, for instance, if we refer to table 7 on page 17, and we see Muslims employees, then next category is Muslims owners, and next one, self-employed and help, and we then look for men and women at the XB values, we see the numbers, approximately, 4.7, 5.9, 6.1. These are the numbers. So these numbers tell us how many times the risk of, for instance, Muslims employees were higher than the risk for inactive others. It is just a comparison of these two groups, one being a reference, the same reference for all other categories.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But you did not, if I may, you did not make that same calculation with respect to each of the occupational status, namely, employees, owners, or self-employed and help; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Separately, you mean, as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Using the --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This model that we are discussing is a so-called interaction model. This means that we look at the effects of being of a given ethnicity and, at the same time, of belonging to a particular occupational group. So it's answer to your question, whether I looked separately at the various occupational categories: No, I didn't, not in this model.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Does your report or conclusions in any way give us an indication of what the intellectuals, if you will, and looking only at occupational status - we'll get to educational attainment in a second - the intellectuals or leadership of the community, whether or not they were targeted?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, it is -- generally, if you make an analysis by socio-economic status, in whatever way the status is measured, you basically want to identify patterns in intensity of a process, like missing or being killed, for the particular categories of the measure used in the study. And, well, how to measure whether or one is a member of the elite or not is of course a very difficult question. One can think of intellectual elite, and then the education is probably not such a bad measure. You can also think that elite are those who cumulated certain material goods more relatively to others. And then you can think of distinguishing owners from employees or inactive, whose income is certainly lowest among all occupational groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: All I'm suggesting is that you did not do any such calculation or analysis; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: You mean the risks of being killed or going missing for the elite from Prijedor? This is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I believe -- I didn't certainly attempt to measure the risk for the elite because the elite can be defined in many, many various ways, and I didn't make any study of whether my definition is a proper one, whether it really measures being a member of the elite in Prijedor. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In part, I agree with you. But in your answer earlier you did say that you looked as factor education, and that can be considered. Your report does address at least arguably education as a possible factor or educational attainment to determine whether or not intellectuals or the elite were targeted, and your conclusion is, based upon a reasonable degree of scientific, statistical, and demographic certainty, that you could not find any such pattern; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Not for education.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My question is for occupation. The same question: You did not in your report, based upon the four or five categories under occupational socio-economic status were you able to determine a pattern based upon whether or not intellectuals were targeted; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Based on occupation, I believe I did find a pattern, systematic pattern of a sort of selection.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What do you mean by sort of selection?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, if you observe, if you see, if you obtain risks, increasing risks associated with the increasing categories in the occupational status, then it is quite obvious that this is the pattern, and we -- I actually saw this pattern, not only for Muslims but also for other ethnic non-Serb groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But from my understanding, you did not use owners in your logistical regression table and compare it to the other categories. What you did is actually use, which is reasonable in my opinion, because it's a rural area, you used two separate categories, namely, self-employed, which I think we can agree means farmers; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, self-employed with help, farmers and their families.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right. And that was my next question. "With help" really means the farmer with the people within that same household assisting him and maintaining and cultivating the land; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So it's that group that you've identified that was targeted; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Not only that group, but two groups, owners and self-employed with help. I think I'm speaking about these two group. These two groups are those who have the upper occupational status, and I believe possessed certain material, certain property, simply, property. This is what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I want to just understand it. So an employee, for example, like a president of a municipal assembly, if he's within the category of employee, you would not be able to quantify for us whether or not that person was targeted; correct, because, utilizing your logistical regression model, you totally excluded that category of socio-economic status under occupations, that category; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: The part about logistical regression is incorrect. How the person, the president, would be classified, whether an employee, he would be an employee or an owner, it depends. If he owned, being the president, also a private firm or a shop or a farm, he would be probably reported not as an employee but as an owner or a self-employed -- self-employed, I don't think so. As an owner, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Or he might be identified as both, and then we would have the problem that we discussed before, and that is of double-counting; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No, no, no. These type of situations, double answers given to the same question, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So what assumptions did you make, if you could quantify them for me, that within the categories that you looked under self-employed and help to self-employed were these individuals also under the category of employees?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, it is -- I don't think so. These persons who reported themselves as self-employed or helping self-employed persons would be reported as self-employed or help. However, it is possible that the person helping a self-employed person reported himself or herself as inactive on the different item, the ZAN variable. We actually believe that this is very well possible because these two items show empirically certain overlap. And in cases, overlapping cases, we gave priority to the report obtained for the PZAN variable, this means that those who were report themselves as inactive and, at the same time, as helping the self-employed, would be taken as help to self-employed in this study.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And then reaching your conclusion that there seems to be a pattern of targeting of that group, can you tell us -- I mean, we know that you relied on these secondary sources, if you will, and you also relied on the census exclusively to provide you with that information; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This information for this part of the study, socio-economic study, comes from the census and is based on the links of those missing, killed, with that census.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On page 4 of your report, you identify a term that I'm unfamiliar with. I think it's in the last paragraph, "Quasi-independent sources." Can you tell me what that means?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Quasi-independent sources. These are the sources that are not fully independent. So there is some degree of dependency of the sources that cannot be expressed quantitatively in terms of correlation measure or something, but we expect that the sources are dependent, and accordingly, we can modify the formulas used for capture-recapture method.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you would include in those sources what as being quasi-independent?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, it is that a person reported missing, for example, in the ICRC list. We think it's likely to be found in mass graves or a declaration of death for such a person that is more likely to be obtained.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you factor in Mr. Sebire's report the number of mass graves versus the number of individual graves to make an assumption as to whether or not those individuals may have died under any of the three items that we discussed, namely, the accidental hump or the mortality within a community or municipality of natural or unrelated causes?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: So you are speaking about causes?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Causes of death?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I must say, I did not study causes of death. To a certain extent, this information is available from the exhumation database, from an item called circumstances of death. The reports, however, are very unstandardised, so it is -- the circumstances tell us something about the situation a person died. Sometimes it can be used to conclude that this was a violent death. In most cases, it was violent deaths and the person was killed, and someone, an eyewitness, saw it. But we didn't study causes of death, due to the lack of standardisation, say, of the reports we had at our disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If the exhumation reports have a specific line item which would permit the person filling out the proof of death, such as circumstances of death, and if you're giving testimony before this Tribunal as to the number of deaths and to determine targeting, isn't cause of death a significant issue for a demographer, such as yourself, to determine?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Of course. Cause of death is a very important item. And if I would be able, I would certainly do so. But first of all, regarding missing persons, it is highly likely that all these people reported as missing are dead and died of violent causes of death. This is what ICRC themselves say about the nature of the disappearances reported in their lists. This is one thing. Well, the deaths coming from court declarations, it is all violent deaths or circumstances unclear. But for those with unclear circumstances, it is missing as the cause of death, which is the same situation this person is missing and the body was never found. But there were people who saw the person taken by some persons against the will of the person, and since then no one has seen this person. So it is -- even though I did not study the causes explicitly, I assumed that the causes of death or disappearance were violent, were not natural. And I am convinced that this is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Within the OTP demographic section, if there is such a section --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: There is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is that information readily available on a CD-ROM or disk, both the exhumations as well as the ICRC report? Is that available --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Electronic format, you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Of course. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So if I were to ask the Court or someone to provide that to another demographer if they were interested to look at it to determine the cause of death, that would be something that you can provide or your department can provide to me in a CD form correct? Or an electronic version?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes. ICRC list is publicly available from the Internet, so you do not have to request this list from anyone. The Knjiga Nestalih, I think, is available electronically, and those who published it can share this information with you. As to Exhumations and Proof of Death databases, I think the question must be addressed to those who established the databases.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will. I'm just asking if it's available in an electronic form that's all, and it is right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And also --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: But if I may add something. It is a complex database, so it is not just one single list of names and date of death. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Really what I'm actually -- let me just narrow it down if I may with the Court's permission. The proof of death or the certificate of death as it is called in numerous places is a page or two pages in length. What happens in essence is that you scan that material and then it creates a database of all the exhumations and proof of death from the Bosnian Federation courts; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, it is not necessarily scanned. It is -- the data is entered by some entry personnel and it is just making electronic lists based on the documentation that exists as hard copies, as reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And also the 1991 census is available in electronic form; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And now let me ask you, based on your prior -- just now your answer, if I recollect it correctly: You made an assumption that the exhumations and the report of proof of death, that you're assuming that those were of violent deaths; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And in fact - there's no dispute about that - if you look, your number on the exhumations for the data as a source was 960. That's what we have exactly. However, you use 1.731 as the number of missing or dead persons; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: One correction. The 960 was incorrect number. I corrected it earlier today, and it is 638, 638. And the number 1.731 is the number obtained not only on the basis of Exhumations and Proof of Death databases, but also lists of missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What I'm suggesting to you is this: If I were to ask you or another demographer to take a specific item such as the exhumations and do an analysis to determine whether there was targeting, the best possible way to do that is to take the number of 638, which are the established proof of deaths by virtue of violent means, and then make your calculation and tables based upon that, instead of using what I consider, respectfully, Dr. Tabeau, a grossly overinflated number of 1.731, which is almost three times the number of those reported in the Federation courts. Would that be a way that someone can do it?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't do this in this way, because you restrict your analysis to information obtained from exhumations and court rulings, which we know is very much incomplete, and you should include as much information as possible. And this is what we did. We analysed the other total, because this is the way to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When you say "incomplete," you really mean it's unreliable and inaccurate; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: No. Incomplete, I mean -- means that many records are excluded, are not there, not in this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's all the questions we have, Your Honour. Thank you very much. Thank you, Dr. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a final clarification. We had already an extended discussion on this number 1.731, and I would ask when, for future purposes, maybe in the case of Defence, you shouldn't take it as given that the legal relevance of these numbers has such a high importance, as it was stated in former decisions. Maybe this Chamber, as already indicated, may come to other solutions and to other definitions. And we have to be aware what we are discussing here. We are discussing the alleged genocide, and I wonder if it's the real and concrete and most appropriate approach to discuss this on the basis of figures only. The term we have to discuss is whether or not there was an intent, and does it really change whether the number is 1.700 or 2.300?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Having said this, only one question: It was discussed whether or not there were other peoples included in this number of 1.731. You stated this would be the absolute minimum; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It was discussed, from the point of view of the Defence, no doubt correctly, what about the question: Is it an overstatement? But can you please tell me: In how far are other persons included in this number, and how does it affect this number? For example, we heard on several occasions earlier from witnesses that we had visitors coming to Prijedor, and no doubt not included in the former census, and then allegedly later become witnesses in this tragedy in Prijedor. What would be the impact on your numbers of persons, and did you take these additional persons into account? Because it would maybe affect the question of the percentage.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: We only looked at the population who originally lived in Prijedor in 1991 and was reported in that census, and only events related to this population were analysed in this report. So if a visitor went missing, for instance, or was killed, it is not included in this study.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this. And one second -- just for my own clarification, help me with this: Given the example a person was killed in the municipality of Sanski Most and, for what reason whatsoever, found his or her grave in Prijedor, was this included in the number of persons you identified in your report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: If this person killed in Sanski Most would be reported as part of Prijedor population in 1991 census --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Say this person -- yes. I don't know whether there was such a census in 1991 also in, say, Sanski Most. And this person, to give an example, was killed by whomsoever in the municipality of Sanski Most but then later on buried in a grave or a mass grave in Prijedor. In how far is this included in your report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: This is all about where the person lived in 1991. If this was someone from the Prijedor municipality, killed in Sanski Most and buried in a grave in Prijedor, the person would be reported, would be reported in our study, if, of course, the person -- the record will be linked with that census. So it is that we actually tried to trace individuals from Prijedor municipality from 1991, their fate. We tried to estimate, to calculate, how many of them just died or went missing. And we know that most of them, almost all of them, died or went missing in the municipality of Prijedor. This is what our study is reporting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. We discussed already the question how to define "elite," and I was to a certain extent alerted when you mentioned this morning - and you do it in your report on page 11 - that you cannot see an obvious pattern of targeting related to the educational categories. Could you please give some more details on this, your statement.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I suggest to look at figures 4A and 4B on page 12. This is next page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: -- of the report. These two figures are made on the basis of the numbers included in tables 5A and 5B. These are the same figures. It is easier to see, to analyse numbers, by looking at the figures. Figure 4A shows the risk of going missing or being killed for each ethnic group separately by, at the same time, educational attainment, or by education simply, by education, completed education. If we take as an example the curve shown for Croats, the blue one, then we see a very clear pattern, with low risks obtained for those with no education and incomplete elementary education, and slowly increasing risks for those with elementary education, secondary education, and highest risk for those with post-secondary education. This is the blue curve for Croats. If this type of pattern would be obtained for all other non-Serb ethnic groups, we could speak about a pattern of selection in the missing process and killing of the population. But if we look at the curve for Muslims, the green one, the uppermost one, then we see that those with no education or incomplete elementary indeed have lower risks of being killed or missing. Then elementary, those with elementary and secondary education, have elevated risks, clearly. But the risk for those with post-secondary education is not higher than the risk for those with elementary and secondary. It is actually a little bit lower. If we then continue this type of observation with figure 4B, where only men are shown, so the curve for Muslims is even more irregular. The highest risk is only seen for those with elementary education. In my view, it only confirms what we see also in other distributions of the population, that the group who most frequently were killed and went missing were men with relatively low level of education, elementary level of education, and in eight groups from, say, 20 to 49, which are most active military ages. So for men it would be a different mechanism, I think, than educationally related targeting. But as I said, elite is something that can be defined in very many different ways, and measuring this is a very challenging task to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If not, even impossible, because no doubt it could be related to high position, low position. You can discuss rich and poor, occupation and so on. But I think this was covered. Only one last question on the basis of a question by Mr. Koumjian. Is there any hint or any information, reliable information, you obtained that higher-educated-persons were "smart enough to leave Prijedor before detained."

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: I don't have ready answer right now, but this can be investigated. We could analyse the education level of those who left the country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And in case if it would be needed, you would have the information who left the country between 1991 and then until 1992? Would this be possible?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU
utterances.text: Well, we don't have information for this particular period, but an analysis could be presented quickly on the basis of the voters register, which reports people living abroad by 1997, which is a distant period from the period we are discussing here. But I believe we could use a sample from a country like the Netherlands or a Scandinavian country like Sweden and we could request lists of refugees from Bosnia and Herzegovina and analyse educational level of those persons for this period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No doubt insofar as the burden of proof is with the Prosecutor, and from our side there will be no such request, taking into account all the possibilities, difficulties with these numbers. May I ask Judge Fassi Fihri, any additional questions? No questions. There are no other questions emanating from my questions. This is not the case. Then I have to thank you for your entire report and the additional information you gave to us. And may I ask the usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom. In the meantime, unfortunately, I have to use two more minutes. First, the Status Conference this afternoon, are there any objections by the parties as regards the presence of Judge Vassylenko during the Status Conference?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The Bench decided not to admit, at least not today, the provisional marked Exhibit S338. No doubt there was no possibility for the Defence to go into details of this document in the framework of cross-examination. But most important is we should really concentrate on Dr. Tabeau's report on Prijedor only, and therefore we don't see the added value of this report, and therefore this is not admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Finally, I read out this morning my report to the Chamber on the Rule 71(E). This document will be admitted -- or is admitted into evidence as -- let me know CJ14, J14. And then this morning I asked the parties whether there are any objections how to proceed on the admission of evidence as suggested in this report. I have heard no additional objections than those we can find in the transcripts, and therefore all these documents listed in this report are hereby admitted into evidence under the numbers you can read in this report. This concludes today's hearing. The Court resumes tomorrow, 9.30, in this courtroom. And a Status Conference in this case will be held as from 2.30 this afternoon, also in this courtroom.
